verdict.rationale: Homebrew documents one package manager and one Brewfile workflow across macOS, Linux and WSL, with one command to set up dependencies across these environments and CI, and Brewfiles can manage WinGet packages from WSL. Windows support is only through WSL, not native Windows. Community reports note Linux friction, such as the /home/linuxbrew requirement for bottles and brittleness on CI. Missing for 10: native Windows support outside WSL, evidence that Brewfile entries such as casks and Mac App Store apps behave consistently across OSes, and independent corroboration of seamless cross-OS parity.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use the same workflow and config on macOS, Linux, and Windows

citations.quote: Use the same package manager to manage your macOS, Linux and Windows systems
Homebrew installs the command-line tools and applications you need across macOS, Linux and WSL.
one command can set up project dependencies across these environments and in continuous-integration services such as GitHub Actions.
you can also use `brew bundle` with casks, taps, Mac App Store apps, WinGet packages on WSL
